sections.name: Devtools IaC + GitOps
description: As a devops team managing many internal tools, we built this to accelerate development with a self-hosted AWS environment — fully customizable and modeled after our real internal setup, not a stripped-down sandbox.
The foundation is identity and data: a Windows AD domain controller paired with RHBK (Keycloak) for OIDC, and a shared Postgres database on RDS — the same primitives every devtool on top depends on.
The devtools themselves (Jira, Bitbucket, Confluence, Artifactory, ArgoCD, Xray) are layered on top of that foundation, standing up a complete environment with effectively one click.
Foundation and devtools alike are provisioned and kept in sync purely through IaC (Terraform/Terragrunt) and GitOps (ArgoCD auto-syncing from Git) — nothing is ever applied by hand.

repos.name: Documentation
repos.description: Published architecture and bootstrap docs for the whole Devtools IaC + GitOps platform — explains all the infra we have (EKS, RDS, domain controller, Cloudflare, backups) and every repo in this section (aws-terraform-bootstrap, devtools-labs, clusters-provision/definition, devtools-provision/definition) and how they fit together.

repos.name: aws-terraform-bootstrap
repos.description: Step 1, once per AWS account: one-time Terraform that creates the shared S3 bucket used for Terragrunt remote state across all projects — must exist before devtools-labs can apply.

repos.name: devtools-labs
repos.description: Step 2: Terraform + Terragrunt that provisions a multi-node EKS cluster and bootstraps ArgoCD inside it — plus the RDS instance, Windows AD domain controller, Cloudflare DNS/Access, and AWS Backup coverage the platform needs. Once ArgoCD is up, its two ApplicationSets auto-discover and auto-sync every cluster-infra tool and devtool (ingress, secrets sync, tunnel, Jira, Bitbucket, Confluence, Artifactory, ArgoCD) — none of it is ever applied by hand.

repos.name: clusters-provision
repos.description: Helm charts for the cluster-wide infrastructure the platform runs on — ingress-nginx, external-secrets-operator, cloudflared, and the RHBK OIDC identity provider. The "what to deploy" half of a provision/definition pair, auto-discovered by ArgoCD's clusters-applicationset.

repos.name: clusters-definition
repos.description: Environment-specific Helm values overrides for clusters-provision, plus the clusters-applicationset itself. Deploys first so devtools (e.g. Bitbucket's ExternalSecret) never race the infra they depend on.

repos.name: devtools-provision
repos.description: Umbrella Helm charts for the self-hosted devtools platform — Jira, Bitbucket, Confluence, Artifactory, ArgoCD, and Xray Data Center editions. The "what to deploy" half of a provision/definition pair, auto-discovered by ArgoCD's devtools-applicationset.

repos.name: devtools-definition
repos.description: Environment-specific Helm values overrides for devtools-provision, plus the devtools-applicationset itself — ingress hosts, shared RDS credentials, and per-tool resource sizing.

sections.name: Platform
description: Wrapper APIs that sit in front of all our tools — Bitbucket, Jira, Confluence, SonarQube, Artifactory, ArgoCD — so they're provisioned and managed through one consistent interface instead of each tool's own console.
In the org environment, those APIs are called through approval-request templates built on Backstage, rather than being hit directly.

repos.name: devops-api
repos.description: FastAPI service that self-service-provisions devtool resources: Bitbucket/Jira projects, Confluence spaces, SonarQube groups, and Artifactory projects (each with create + admin/user-group assignment + rollback-on-failure), plus ArgoCD GitOps consumer-config and cluster-secret management. Bitbucket is the source of truth; this GitHub copy is a read-only mirror kept in sync by a Woodpecker pipeline on every Bitbucket push.

repos.name: apis-library
repos.description: Shared Python library with async connectors for AWX, ArgoCD, Bitbucket, and Vault, plus a reusable FastAPI application factory.

sections.name: CI/CD
description: Custom semantic-versioning and CHANGELOG automation for every Docker image our CI/CD pipelines build, driven by conventional commits rather than manual tagging.
Also customizes third-party images by baking in the internal CA, so outside images can be pulled and run inside the org's network over TLS.

repos.name: a-woodpecker-plugins
repos.description: MasterVersions — a stateless release orchestrator (`release.py`) that automates semantic versioning and CHANGELOG generation for polyrepo, monorepo, and nested-monorepo repo layouts. The PR body is the single source of truth: conventional-commit lines (`feat(scope): msg`, wildcards, `!` for breaking) decide which components get tagged and what bump level, with commit-type recognition driven entirely by `cliff.toml`. Read-only GitHub mirror; source of truth is Bitbucket, synced one-way by a Woodpecker pipeline on every push.

repos.name: inbound-images
repos.description: The org's own base images and Woodpecker plugins — real content, versioned independently per component (VERSION.txt) using the same commit-message grammar as a-woodpecker-plugins.

repos.name: outbound-images-with-ca
repos.description: Hardened copies of upstream images we didn't author, wrapped only with the internal CA so they can reach *.devopstashtiot.page over TLS. Everything shares one version, bumped only when the CA rotates.

sections.name: SaaS
description: Packages the org's own tooling (ArgoCD, Woodpecker) as a service other teams can onboard onto, instead of each team standing up and maintaining their own instance.

repos.name: argocd
repos.description: 🚧 In development, not yet operational. Per-consumer ArgoCD onboarding configs (imported from the old Bitbucket ARGO project) plus the cluster-secret Helm chart that generates an ArgoCD cluster Secret for each entry in applicationClusters.

repos.name: woodpecker
repos.description: 🚧 In development, not yet operational. Per-consumer Woodpecker onboarding configs (imported from the old Bitbucket ARGO project), one directory per team requesting CI access.

sections.name: Automation
description: Small automations that exist purely to make day-to-day life simpler for our organization's staff members — syncing data and alerting on the repetitive chores nobody wants to do by hand.

repos.name: aws-xray-db-sync
repos.description: Lambda that runs every minute to sync JFrog Xray offline DB bundles to S3, with SNS alerts on success or failure.

sections.name: AWS Environment & Governance
description: Documents the AWS environment this org actually runs on — the guardrails in place (Control Tower SCPs, IAM role boundaries), the architecture (VPC, IRSA pod identity for EKS, Windows Server RDP access), and governance anomalies found while working in the account — so nobody has to rediscover them the hard way.

repos.name: AWS Environment Docs
repos.description: Documents this AWS account's guardrails and how the environment is actually built: Control Tower SCPs and what they block (e.g. GuardDuty/VPC peering denied), IAM role boundaries, IRSA pod identity for EKS, VPC architecture, Windows Server RDP access, and governance anomalies found while probing the account. Published on this same site (devops-tashtiot.github.io), which doubles as the GitHub Pages landing page guiding another devops team through every repo in this organization.
